mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over the prior 6 months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 6 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 6-month change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which anticipates higher corporate profits and drives S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points within the same month
failure_condition: Multivariate Granger causality test rejects PAYEMS leading UNRATE in predicting SPX 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, investors anticipate future rate hikes, causing a short-term discount in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns show no negative correlation with CPIAUCSL monthly surprise (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests improving supply conditions that reduce supply-side bottlenecks, which typically supports corporate earnings and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Regression of SPX 20-day returns on INDPRO lags shows R-squared < 0.02 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1%, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which typically boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases month-over-month for 3 consecutive months while UNRATE remains flat or falls
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns show no predictive power from the PAYEMS/UNRATE interaction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in retail sales (not available in provided proxies - skip this one to stay compliant) — instead, use HOUST as a proxy for business activity: A 2% month-over-month decline in HOUST coinciding with a 0.1% drop in CPIAUCSL suggests demand softening, which can depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change < -2% and CPIAUCSL monthly change < -0.1%
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positively correlated with the combined HOUST/CPIAUCSL shock (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 240) combined with a strong labor market (PAYEMS > 150,000), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative due to expectations of future rate hikes and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: In the specified regime, SPX 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).
